ocr.notes: Minor wording error: 'managed to get away from Sullivan' should be 'managed to keep away from Sullivan'.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch printed Tom Allen's view of the Mitchell–Sullivan fight: Charley Mitchell dodged and winded Sullivan, though one good blow from a fresh Sullivan would have ended it in the second round.

metadata.notes: No page image; date and paper taken from the file name (St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday, March 11, 1888). The section is one of several local reactions to the news of the fight.

facts.fact: Allen, called the ex-champion, gave his opinion of the Mitchell–Sullivan fight, crediting Mitchell's dodging for winding Sullivan
facts.quote: My ideas of the fight are that Mitchell, who is one of the cleverest dodgers in the ring, managed to keep away from Sullivan for a good while and winded the big fellow. ... If Sullivan could have got one good crack at Mitchell while fresh the fight would have stopped in the second round.

notes: The clipping does not name the fight's date or place; it is presumably the Sullivan–Mitchell fight in France on March 10, 1888, but that is not stated in the text. Focus suggested secondary because this is one section of a larger round-up of reactions.
